items.title: Live: Chance of August rate hike tumbles as inflation cools
items.description: The big focus locally is the consumer price index and what it will mean for interest rates. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Motorists to lose fuel discount from Monday
items.description: Drivers will lose the fuel excise discount as planned, despite escalating pressure on global oil prices and warnings the world has depleted reserves.

items.title: Without more oil, a new refinery makes no sense
items.description: Experts say a new refinery would need to use imported oil and question how it would be competitive.

items.title: Deaths of woman and toddler being treated as murder-suicide, police say
items.description: South Australia Police say they are treating the deaths of a woman and her toddler found in water off the state’s south-east coast as a murder-suicide.

items.title: Family embroiled in decades-old IVF mix-up files lawsuit against hospital
items.description: The biological parents of twins who were born after an IVF embryo mix-up at Royal North Shore Hospital in Sydney have launched civil action.

items.title: Japanese mall had just reopened before earthquake and explosion
items.description: Before the magnitude-7.1 earthquake hit, the mall had highlighted its seismically reinforced ceilings and improvements to safety and ⁠resilience.

items.title: Judge slams law firm over delayed $120m payout to sacked Qantas staff
items.description: Maurice Blackburn Lawyers has been handling a $120 million payout that Qantas agreed to pay its illegally sacked workers in 2024, with a judge rebuking the delayed compensation.

items.title: Taylor denies giving money to group at centre of NSW corruption probe
items.description: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption has seen a series of text messages in which key figures discuss a plan to "shake down" Angus Taylor for financial support.

items.title: Presumed dead, 'Doctor Jihad' gave a revealing interview about life under ISIS
items.description: An Australian man dubbed "Dr Jihad" claims he never intended to join Islamic State and never pledged allegiance to the extremist organisation, in a recently resurfaced interview.

items.title: US and Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed militants after 'surprise attack'
items.description: Fresh fighting has erupted after the US accused Iran of launching its first ballistic missile attack on an American base since strikes were paused on Friday. Here's your three-minute briefing on the key developments in the Middle East overnight.

items.title: Local transmission of H5 bird flu 'very, very likely', SA government says
items.description: A further 11 suspected cases of H5 bird flu have been detected in South Australia’s south-east and Kangaroo Island.

items.title: China's singing sailors could be latest weapon in fight for South China Sea
items.description: China's state media releases an English version of a love ballad about lovesick sailors in the South China Sea.

items.title: 'They are getting fooled': How ultra-processed food is made to look healthier
items.description: Industry insiders reveal how Australians are being deceived by marketing and labelling that makes ultra-processed foods appear healthier than they really are.

items.title: What belongs in your FOGO bin? Definitely not Ozempic needles
items.description: A north-west Tasmanian waste management company says it has a $700,000 per year problem, and council ratepayers are picking up the tab.

items.title: Men on why they are choosing not to have children
items.description: What readers have to say about being childfree after our story on why more men are turning away from fatherhood.

items.title: Miles Franklin shortlist defies 'shaggy' trend in Australian publishing
items.description: ABC experts unpack the shortlist of Australia's biggest book prize: who made it, who missed out and who they think will win.

items.title: This show is like James Bond, except it’s a comedy set in New Zealand
items.description: What happens when you take the exciting world of spies and subterfuge to 1970s New Zealand? We talk to Paul Williams and Bret McKenzie about making their childhood fantasies come true in hilarious new comedy.

items.title: Quick hits: Record beaten five times in 10 minutes, pool haka thrills
items.description: New Zealand swimmers pay tribute to a victorious teammate, a lawn bowler fits in some work shifts and a weightlifting record falls a staggering five times. Here are the quick hits from day five of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: Live: New premier under attack from opposition MP, who struggles to recall his name
items.description: Questions are swirling around the details of Ben Carroll's freshly announced royal commission into the construction sector, as the new Victorian premier starts his first full day in the job.

items.title: Senior Liberals tried to damage career of former minister, ICAC told
items.description: The NSW corruption watchdog has heard senior Liberal Party operatives created a document in alleged attempts to damage the career of former minister David Elliott.

items.title: Doctors tell royal commission political advocacy has no place in healthcare
items.description: Medical practitioners should be prohibited from wearing political pins to prevent patients from feeling unsafe, the royal commission on antisemitism has heard.

items.title: Angus Taylor likes to talk about systems. People are his 'kryptonite'
items.description: In an interview for Kitchen Cabinet, the opposition leader recalls feeling a sense of overwhelm and reverence for the parliament when first he took his seat there.

items.title: Banks slammed for failing to pick up mortgage offset problems
items.description: The corporate regulator found Australian banks paid more than $55 million in compensation in just two years, for failures with mortgage offset accounts, warning customers could be paying more interest than they should.

items.title: Public servant charged over alleged multi-million dollar fraud of NDIS
items.description: A 39-year-old Darwin woman is charged with using her position with the Department of Children and Families to defraud the NDIS of millions of dollars.

items.title: 'Australia's Banksy' rape case witness wants the courts to hear this
items.description: A woman who accused street artist Anthony Lister of rape is speaking up to help others navigate the police and court systems. Lister was acquitted of all charges last year.
